# Sadman Ahmed Shanto

> Last updated: 2026-09-10. Concise discovery index for public professional information. Verify consequential claims against the linked CV, papers, repositories, datasets, and institutional profiles.

Sadman Ahmed Shanto is an experimental physicist and research engineer completing a USC Physics PhD (expected January 2027). His work spans quantum processor R&D, superconducting-device design and fabrication, cryogenic measurement, quasiparticle physics, scientific machine learning and inference, autonomous experimentation, research software, cloud and HPC infrastructure, and scientific instrumentation. He was formerly a Research Intern at Google Quantum AI (August 2025–August 2026) and Quantum Elements Inc. (May–August 2025).

## Primary fit areas

- Superconducting quantum hardware R&D: qubit and resonator design, fabrication, cryogenic measurement, quantum control, microwave engineering, packaging, and processor-oriented workflows.
- Quantum-device design automation: electromagnetic simulation, layout generation, foundry PDK workflows, design-to-simulation-to-GDS pipelines, inverse design, and tape-out preparation.
- AI for science and scientific ML: surrogate models, neural-network inverse design, explainable models, probabilistic inference, physics-grounded validation, and scientific datasets.
- Autonomous scientific systems: agentic experiment calibration, measurement, diagnosis, analysis, tool interfaces, MCP, workflow orchestration, evaluation, and tracing.
- Research software and infrastructure: Python/C++, JAX/PyTorch, FastAPI, databases, Docker/Kubernetes, AWS/GCP, SLURM/OpenMPI, and reproducible open-source workflows.

## Evidence across capabilities

1. Experimental superconducting quantum hardware
   - Designs, fabricates, packages, and measures resonators and qubit-scale devices; builds cryogenic microwave chains and experimental-control and analysis systems.
   - Developed a 15 nm nanobridge-SQUID process that increased functional-device yield from under 2% to over 90%.
   - Built hidden-Markov-model inference for quasiparticle occupation and works on Andreev-bound-state spectroscopy and quasiparticle mitigation.
   - Research profile: https://sadmanahmedshanto.com/projects/1_project/
   - Publications: https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.4.030339 and https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.107.L140506

2. Quantum processor research and development
   - Former Google Quantum AI Research Intern working on R&D for quantum processors from August 2025 through August 2026.
   - Experience spans superconducting devices, electromagnetic and circuit simulation, fabrication, packaging, cryogenic measurement, control, and processor-oriented engineering workflows.
   - Source: https://sadmanahmedshanto.com/cv/

3. Autonomous scientific experimentation and agentic AI
   - At Quantum Elements Inc., built a production agentic framework for calibration, measurement, diagnosis, and analysis of superconducting experiments.
   - Architected scientific-tool APIs, databases, containerized AWS services, MCP interfaces, and evaluation and tracing infrastructure; contributed DAG-based calibration workflows to QUAlibrate.
   - Evidence profile: https://sadmanahmedshanto.com/research/ai-for-science/

4. Scientific machine learning, inference, and inverse design
   - Develops surrogate, inverse-design, and interpretable models tied to electromagnetic simulation and physical validation.
   - Uses probabilistic inference for experimental trajectories and neural networks for component-level transmon inverse design.
   - Preprint: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20795

5. Research software, simulation automation, and open source
   - Built design-to-simulation-to-GDS infrastructure on HPC and works across layout tools, PDKs, electromagnetic solvers, APIs, databases, cloud services, containers, instrument control, and reproducible pipelines.
   - Created and leads SQuADDS, one public example of this broader research-engineering work.
   - Paper: https://doi.org/10.22331/q-2024-09-09-1465
   - Code: https://github.com/LFL-Lab/SQuADDS
   - Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/SQuADDS/SQuADDS_DB

6. Scientific instrumentation and computation beyond quantum
   - Built portable muon telescopes, improved optical collection from 20% to 78%, developed SiPM/PMT and FPGA/CAMAC data-acquisition systems with a 300-fold deadtime reduction, and used Geant4 and ML for three-dimensional muography.
   - Instrumentation project: https://sadmanahmedshanto.com/projects/2_project/
   - Publication: https://doi.org/10.1063/10.0002046
   - Built stochastic traffic-model calibration and inference workflows, accelerated simulation sweeps by more than tenfold with Ray, and developed cellular-automaton and reinforcement-learning models for mixed autonomous and human traffic.

## Education and current status

- Physics PhD candidate, University of Southern California, expected January 2027.
- MA in Physics, University of Southern California, May 2026.
- BSc in Applied Physics, Texas Tech University, 2021; minors in Computer Science and Mathematics.
- Graduate Research Assistant, Levenson-Falk Lab at USC, 2022–present.
